protocols.name: Quiet sitting
protocols.posture: Seated upright, feet flat, knees about 90 degrees, hands on lap, no talking
protocols.rationale: Establishes a seated rest baseline for the three quadriceps channels so later contraction and gait trials can be compared against true quiet EMG.
protocols.interpretation: All three channels (VL, VM, RF) should stay near the noise floor with no rhythmic bursts; spikes that track posture shifts or phone handling are motion artifact, not muscle drive.

protocols.name: Quiet standing
protocols.posture: Comfortable quiet stance, feet roughly hip-width, arms at sides, eyes open, gaze fixed ahead
protocols.rationale: Captures postural background on VL, biceps femoris, and medial gastrocnemius before dynamic tasks that add push-off or co-contraction.
protocols.interpretation: Expect low, fairly steady activity; brief rises on medial gastrocnemius or VL with sway are normal. Large transient spikes that match foot shifts or cable tug are artifact.

protocols.name: Seated leg extension
protocols.posture: Seated, knee about 90 degrees, arms crossed, back supported if needed; extend one knee at a time
protocols.rationale: Isolates knee-extensor drive on VL, VM, and RF with clear left and right effort markers for side-to-side comparison.
protocols.interpretation: During each extend phase, VL, VM, and RF on the tested side should rise together; relax phases should fall toward baseline. Cross-talk or delayed fall may indicate incomplete relaxation or cable motion.

protocols.name: Walking
protocols.posture: Overground level walking at a comfortable self-selected pace; phone secured; clear straight path
protocols.rationale: Records cyclic VL, biceps femoris, and medial gastrocnemius timing across stance and swing for a short, phone-friendly bout.
protocols.interpretation: Expect VL rise around loading/stance, biceps femoris activity into late swing or early stance, and medial gastrocnemius rise in late stance push-off. Flat lines during walking suggest electrode loss; huge broadband spikes suggest foot strike artifact.

protocols.name: Running
protocols.posture: Short overground jog on a clear path; self-selected easy pace; soft landings if possible
protocols.rationale: A brief running bout stresses push-off and swing-related activity on the thigh-and-calf montage without needing a long continuous run.
protocols.interpretation: Compared with walking, expect higher amplitude and shorter bursts on VL and medial gastrocnemius, with biceps femoris contributing in swing. Check that channels return toward quieter levels after stop; prolonged high noise may be electrode bounce.

protocols.name: Bilateral jump
protocols.posture: Standing, feet hip-width; countermovement jump with both legs; soft landing; arms free for balance
protocols.rationale: Marks countermovement, flight, and landing so VL, hamstring, and calf co-activity can be aligned to propulsion and impact.
protocols.interpretation: Prep/crouch often shows rising VL (and sometimes biceps femoris); push and flight show brief high activity then a quieter flight window; land should show a sharp multi-channel burst. Spikes only on impact without preceding prep may be artifact-dominated.

protocols.name: Single-leg jump
protocols.posture: Standing on the tested leg; small single-leg hop with soft landing; non-tested foot off the ground; spotter if needed
protocols.rationale: Emphasizes unilateral push-off and landing co-contraction on VL, biceps femoris, and medial gastrocnemius with explicit left and right trials.
protocols.interpretation: On the hopped side, expect a clear prep rise, a short high push burst, then a landing co-burst across channels. The resting side is not instrumented here; compare left vs right trials for amplitude and landing settle time.

protocols.name: Single-leg balance
protocols.posture: Single-leg stance, non-stance foot lightly lifted, arms free, eyes open; near a wall for safety
protocols.rationale: Probes sustained postural co-activity and corrective bursts on VL, biceps femoris, and medial gastrocnemius during timed left and right holds.
protocols.interpretation: Expect a step-up in baseline when the single-leg hold starts, then intermittent corrective bursts especially on medial gastrocnemius and VL. A sudden channel dropout or huge DC-like spike often means electrode peel or foot stamp.

protocols.name: Sit-to-stand
protocols.posture: Seated on a firm chair, feet flat about hip-width, arms crossed; stand fully then sit with control
protocols.rationale: Sit-to-stand is a short functional quad-loading task that links seated rest EMG to upright weight acceptance on the knee-extensor montage.
protocols.interpretation: VL, VM, and RF should rise together through the stand phase and ease during controlled sit; channels remaining high while seated again suggest incomplete relaxation or leaning on the thighs.

protocols.name: Squat
protocols.posture: Standing, feet hip-width; bodyweight squat to a comfortable depth (about thigh parallel if able); heels down; arms forward for balance
protocols.rationale: Provides repeated concentric–eccentric quadriceps loading under closed-chain conditions that seated extension does not capture.
protocols.interpretation: All three channels should increase through descent and ascent and fall during stand rests. A single channel staying loud while the others rest often flags poor contact or a stuck cable rather than selective muscle work.

protocols.name: Heel raise
protocols.posture: Standing, feet hip-width, hands lightly on a wall or chair for balance; rise onto both forefeet then lower
protocols.rationale: Isolates plantar-flexion drive on medial gastrocnemius while documenting how little VL and biceps femoris should contribute in a quiet bilateral heel raise.
protocols.interpretation: Medial gastrocnemius should dominate each raise phase; VL and biceps femoris should stay comparatively quiet unless the subject leans or bends the knees. If all three channels explode together, suspect balance recovery or cable motion.

protocols.name: Gait initiation
protocols.posture: Quiet standing, then first step forward with a nominated lead foot into a few walking steps; clear path ahead
protocols.rationale: Captures the quiet-to-first-step transition where anticipatory postural activity and early push-off appear before steady walking.
protocols.interpretation: After baseline, look for a brief preparatory change then a clear medial gastrocnemius and VL rise on the first push/step; biceps femoris may rise into swing of the stepping limb. Compare left-lead and right-lead trials for timing, not pathology labels.

protocols.name: Step-up
protocols.posture: Facing a stable step or box about mid-shin height; step up with the nominated lead leg, bring the trail foot up, then step down with control
protocols.rationale: Step-up loads the lead-limb quadriceps in a functional closed-chain pattern useful when gait space is limited.
protocols.interpretation: Lead-leg extend phases should show coordinated VL, VM, and RF elevation; descend should show a second rise then return toward quiet standing. Asymmetry between left-lead and right-lead trials is for recording QA, not clinical labeling.

protocols.name: Quiet hand
protocols.posture: Seated, both forearms on a table, palms down, fingers slightly flexed, no talking
protocols.rationale: Establishes a quiet baseline for abductor pollicis brevis, first dorsal interosseous, and abductor digiti minimi before grip and finger-abduction trials.
protocols.interpretation: All three channels should stay near the noise floor with no rhythmic bursts. Spikes that track a finger twitch or a cable tug are motion artifact, not resting muscle drive.

protocols.name: Power grip
protocols.posture: Seated, forearm supported on a table; make a firm fist without lifting the forearm
protocols.rationale: Records a co-contraction grasp on the thenar, first dorsal interosseous, and hypothenar channels with separate left and right efforts.
protocols.interpretation: During each grip phase all three channels should rise together and fall when the hand opens. A channel that stays flat through a firm fist often means poor contact. A channel that stays loud through relax means the hand did not open.

protocols.interpretation: Abductor pollicis brevis should dominate each abduct phase. First dorsal interosseous may show some cross-talk; abductor digiti minimi should stay comparatively quiet. If all three channels match exactly, suspect a shared cable artifact.

protocols.name: Index abduction
protocols.posture: Seated, palm down on the table, fingers together; slide the index finger away from the middle finger
protocols.rationale: Targets first dorsal interosseous while abductor pollicis brevis and abductor digiti minimi show how selective the effort is.
protocols.interpretation: First dorsal interosseous should rise on each abduct phase and fall on relax. The thenar and hypothenar channels should stay lower unless the whole hand spreads. Equal bursts on every channel suggest a global fist rather than index abduction.

protocols.rationale: Quiet baseline for biceps brachii and the long and lateral heads of triceps before flexion and extension trials.
protocols.interpretation: All three channels should stay near the noise floor. A steady low biceps hum can be resting tone or poor contact; compare it with the effort trials before calling it muscle drive.

protocols.interpretation: Biceps should rise on each flex phase; both triceps heads should stay quieter unless the subject co-contracts. Relax should return biceps toward baseline. If the triceps channels match the biceps burst, suspect an extension effort or cable motion.
